sections.markdown:
# payment-orchestration-service: circuit breaker resilience

A Spring Boot payment orchestration service calls seven downstream dependencies typical of a bank's payment flow.
Each call is protected by its own **Resilience4j circuit breaker**, and each dependency is simulated with a
**different, realistic failure mode** and a **fallback chosen for how critical it is**. Metrics are exported with
the Micrometer Dynatrace registry.

| Circuit breaker | Dependency | Failure mode simulated | Trips on | Threshold | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `core-banking-ledger` | Mainframe system of record | Slow calls during a batch window | Slow-call rate | 50% of calls > 1.5 s | Stale cached balance; postings queued as pending |
| `fraud-scoring` | Real-time fraud model | Timeouts under load (TimeLimiter 1 s) | Failure rate | 50% | Rules engine: small payments approved, rest to manual review |
| `swift-gateway` | SWIFT cross-border gateway | Random error bursts | Failure rate | 40% | Outbox, replayed while CLOSED (UETR keeps replays idempotent) |
| `notification-service` | SMS / email / push providers | Fails 25-45% every day; rare outages | Failure rate | **80%** (non-critical) | Drop it |
| `customer-profile` | Customer master / KYC | None - healthy baseline | Failure rate | 50% | Cached profile, then fail-safe defaults |
| `sanctions-screening` | Watchlist screening engine | Errors during watchlist reloads | Failure rate | **25%** + Retry | **Fail closed**: payment held for compliance |
| `fx-rates` | FX market data provider | HTTP errors + bad data (stale / off-market quotes) | Failure rate | 50% | Cached rate with wider spread, else refuse; multi-datacenter failover |

## 1. Fleet overview
Where every breaker stands right now, and how much of the timeframe each spent OPEN or HALF_OPEN.

input.value:
timeseries active = max(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.state), by:{name, state}, from:now()-5m, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates"))
| fieldsAdd current = arrayLast(arrayRemoveNulls(active))
| filter current == 1
| fields name, state
| sort name asc

sections.title: Breakers OPEN or HALF_OPEN over time (1 = in that state)

input.value:
timeseries active = max(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.state), by:{name, state},
  filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates")) and (state == "open" or state == "half_open")

sections.title: Share of the timeframe in each state (%)

input.value:
timeseries calls = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), by:{name, kind}, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates"))
| fieldsAdd total = arraySum(calls)
| summarize {
    successful = sum(if(kind == "successful", total)),
    failed = sum(if(kind == "failed", total)),
    ignored = sum(if(kind == "ignored", total))
  }, by:{name}
| lookup [
    timeseries rejected = sum(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.not.permitted.calls), by:{name}, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates"))
    | fieldsAdd notPermitted = arraySum(rejected)
    | fields name, notPermitted
  ], sourceField:name, lookupField:name, fields:{notPermitted}, prefix:"cb."
| fieldsAdd successful = coalesce(successful, 0), failed = coalesce(failed, 0), ignored = coalesce(ignored, 0),
    notPermitted = coalesce(cb.notPermitted, 0)
| fieldsAdd failurePct = round(100.0 * failed / (successful + failed), decimals:1),
    shedPct = round(100.0 * notPermitted / (successful + failed + ignored + notPermitted), decimals:1)
| fields name, successful, failed, ignored, notPermitted, failurePct, shedPct
| sort failurePct desc

sections.markdown:
## 2. Failures and load shedding
Failed calls show the dependency's trouble; **not-permitted** calls are requests the OPEN breaker refused
without calling the dependency at all, answered by its fallback instead. The failure rate is what each breaker
compares with its threshold (points before a breaker has its minimum number of calls are left out).

input.value: timeseries failed = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), by:{name}, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates")) and kind == "failed"

sections.title: Not-permitted calls (shed by an OPEN breaker)

input.value: timeseries notPermitted = sum(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.not.permitted.calls), by:{name}, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates"))

timeseries rate = avg(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.failure.rate), by:{name}, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates"))
| fieldsAdd failureRatePct = iCollectArray(if(rate[] >= 0, rate[]))
| fieldsRemove rate

timeseries {total = sum(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), n = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls)},
  by:{name}, filter:in(name, array("core-banking-ledger", "fraud-scoring", "swift-gateway", "notification-service", "customer-profile", "sanctions-screening", "fx-rates"))
| fieldsAdd avgDurationMs = total[] / n[]
| fieldsRemove total, n

sections.markdown:
## 3. Failure patterns, one breaker at a time

### core-banking-ledger: slow, not broken
The ledger never returns an error. During its batch window most calls take 1.8-4 s, so this breaker opens on its
**slow-call rate** while its failure rate stays at zero.

sections.title: core-banking-ledger: slow-call rate vs failure rate (%)

input.value:
timeseries {slow = avg(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.slow.call.rate), failed = avg(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.failure.rate)},
  filter:name == "core-banking-ledger"
| fieldsAdd slowCallRatePct = iCollectArray(if(slow[] >= 0, slow[])), failureRatePct = iCollectArray(if(failed[] >= 0, failed[]))
| fieldsAdd slowCallThreshold = iCollectArray(if(slow[] >= -1, 50.0))
| fieldsRemove slow, failed

timeseries {total = sum(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), n = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls),
  slowestMs = max(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls)}, filter:name == "core-banking-ledger"
| fieldsAdd avgMs = total[] / n[]
| fieldsRemove total, n

sections.markdown:
### fraud-scoring: timeouts under load
Model latency grows with load during a recurring traffic peak. Past the 1 s **TimeLimiter** the call fails with a
TimeoutException, which the breaker records as a failure. Load ramps up and down, so the breaker opens and then
flaps between HALF_OPEN and CLOSED as the peak drains.

input.value: timeseries calls = sum(resilience4j.timelimiter.calls), by:{kind}, filter:name == "fraud-scoring"

sections.title: fraud-scoring: breaker state (1 = in that state)

input.value:
timeseries active = max(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.state), by:{state},
  filter:name == "fraud-scoring" and (state == "open" or state == "half_open")

sections.markdown:
### swift-gateway: error bursts, and errors that don't count
Bursts of HTTP 503/502 and dropped connections open the breaker. **Validation rejects** (a malformed BIC) are
IGNORED: a bad message says nothing about the gateway's health. Failed payments go to an outbox that is replayed
through the same breaker while it is CLOSED.

input.value: timeseries calls = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), by:{kind}, filter:name == "swift-gateway"

sections.markdown:
### notification-service vs sanctions-screening: thresholds follow criticality
The notification hub fails 25-45% of the time on a normal day and its breaker stays CLOSED, because its threshold
is 80% and a dropped notification costs nothing. Sanctions screening is a compliance control that **fails closed**,
so its breaker opens at 25%.

input.value:
timeseries rate = avg(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.failure.rate), filter:name == "notification-service"
| fieldsAdd failureRatePct = iCollectArray(if(rate[] >= 0, rate[])), threshold = iCollectArray(if(rate[] >= -1, 80.0))
| fieldsRemove rate

timeseries rate = avg(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.failure.rate), filter:name == "sanctions-screening"
| fieldsAdd failureRatePct = iCollectArray(if(rate[] >= 0, rate[])), threshold = iCollectArray(if(rate[] >= -1, 25.0))
| fieldsRemove rate
timeseries calls = sum(resilience4j.retry.calls), by:{kind}, filter:name == "sanctions-screening"

sections.markdown:
### customer-profile: the control line
The healthy baseline. While other breakers open on schedule, this one stays CLOSED, which shows the application
itself is fine and the trouble is in specific dependencies.

input.value: timeseries calls = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), by:{kind}, filter:name == "customer-profile"

sections.markdown:
## 4. Multi-datacenter: fx-rates in prod-us-east-1 and prod-us-east-2
Two instances of the service run as separate datacenters, each with its own `fx-rates` breaker and its own random
market-data feed freezes. A stale or off-market quote is recorded as a failure even though the provider answered
200 OK. The demo client fails over to the other region when the primary can't return a live quote.

> These queries split by the `datacenter` metric dimension, set per instance with
> `management.metrics.tags.datacenter`.

input.value:
timeseries rate = avg(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.failure.rate), by:{datacenter}, filter:name == "fx-rates"
| fieldsAdd failureRatePct = iCollectArray(if(rate[] >= 0, rate[]))
| fieldsRemove rate

sections.title: fx-rates: breaker OPEN by datacenter (1 = open)

input.value: timeseries open = max(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.state), by:{datacenter}, filter:name == "fx-rates" and state == "open"

sections.title: fx-rates: calls by datacenter and outcome

input.value:
timeseries calls = count(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls), by:{datacenter, kind}, filter:name == "fx-rates"
| fieldsAdd total = arraySum(calls)
| summarize {
    successful = sum(if(kind == "successful", total)),
    failed = sum(if(kind == "failed", total))
  }, by:{datacenter}
| lookup [
    timeseries rejected = sum(resilience4j.circuitbreaker.not.permitted.calls), by:{datacenter}, filter:name == "fx-rates"
    | fieldsAdd notPermitted = arraySum(rejected)
    | fields datacenter, notPermitted
  ], sourceField:datacenter, lookupField:datacenter, fields:{notPermitted}, prefix:"cb."
| fieldsAdd successful = coalesce(successful, 0), failed = coalesce(failed, 0), notPermitted = coalesce(cb.notPermitted, 0)
| fieldsAdd failurePct = round(100.0 * failed / (successful + failed), decimals:1)
| fields datacenter, successful, failed, notPermitted, failurePct
